title: Norwich protest against proposed data centre near nature reserve

tea.why: Locals protested against a proposed £1.2bn data centre near a nature reserve, fearing environmental damage.
tea.want: They want to stop the Norwich Apex data centre project from being built near Keswick.
tea.changed: Nov 14-15, 2026: Hundreds gathered in Haymarket, Norwich, to oppose the data centre plans.

summary: Hundreds of people gathered at Haymarket in Norwich to protest against controversial plans by Norwich Apex Ltd for a massive £1.2bn data centre near Keswick. Campaigners raised concerns about the project's proximity to sensitive wildlife habitats, including Marston Marshes, as well as its massive energy and water consumption. Protesters carried signs opposing the facility and voiced fears over potential noise and environmental disruption to local wildlife. In response, Norwich Apex chief executive Matt Bartram stated that environmental protection, acoustic screening, and tree planting were central to the proposal, and emphasized that the facility would create up to 150 permanent jobs while providing essential digital infrastructure.
demands: Stop the Norwich Apex data centre development
Protect nearby nature reserves and wildlife habitats
response: Norwich Apex chief executive Matt Bartram stated that the design prioritizes environmental protection, includes acoustic screening, and features independent ecological assessments to protect nearby nature reserves.

updates.text: Hundreds of people held a demonstration in Norwich against the planned Norwich Apex data centre facility.
Campaigners opposing the development gathered in Haymarket over the weekend to voice concerns.
